analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The visible patch changes the "Last updated" date (line 3) and the GLM video section (head lines 810-813, 829, 876-880). The video text now says variable-frame-rate MP4/QuickTime tracks are indexed rather than refused. Frame i is timed at i / nominalFrameRate, and processor refusals remain deterministic 400s. It also adds template-hash lines around 876-880. The units I examined (base lines 802-1610) show surrounding text unchanged.

The documentation implies a behavior change in the GLM5Next video processor: the variable-frame-rate refusal is removed. The security-relevant bounds in the docs still apply: the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes), the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap, the 2 FPS sampling, and VisionMemoryGate reservations that price the video token ceiling. These keep resource use bounded for DoS (TB-007, T-010, T-029). Frame-by-frame reading of an untrusted VFR track is a new input shape for the decoder. Whether the code still enforces the decode cap and frame-count limits without the CFR check is not visible in the supplied docs. The next pass should confirm it in GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset if source is available. The nominalFrameRate-based timestamp could be skewed by a crafted track, but that affects only timestamp text, not trust boundaries.

The patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false), so the template-hash lines (876-880) are only partly visible. The base text states that GLM LOAD refuses any template other than the shipped one (requireShippedTemplate). Nothing visible suggests this check is weakened. I found no changes to the TB-002 coordinator-provider crypto, A-001 plaintext handling, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or the prefix cache (T-041). There are no security regressions or threat-model invalidations in this docs-only change. I request deeper review only for the code-level video decode bounds, which are outside the supplied evidence.
